Define the Evaluation Scope
Test extrinsic hallucination
Use presumed training-data knowledge
Require concise factual answers

Start from GoodWiki
44,754 good-quality Wikipedia pages
Broad topics and factual content
Public reproducible source pool

Join WikiRank Importance
Use harmonic centrality per page
Proxy training-data frequency
Order head to long-tail knowledge

Create Ten Difficulty Bins
Label levels 0 to 9
Hardest to easiest by centrality
Stabilize dynamic-set difficulty

Sample 5,000 Source Pages
Draw 500 pages from every bin
Balance all difficulty levels
Resample for each dynamic set

Select a Reference Section
Split each article into sections
Randomly choose one section
Keep the source hidden at inference

Generate an Objective Question
Llama 3.1 70B reads the section
Make it specific and self-contained
Require no outside context

Generate the Gold Answer Separately
Answer from the same reference
Separate question and answer stages
Reduce answer leakage into wording

Enforce QA Quality
Require a word or short phrase
Drop answers longer than ten words
Regenerate unanswerable questions

Form the Dynamic Test Set
5,000 question-answer pairs
No fixed public question list
Repeatable difficulty distribution

Query the Tested Model
Provide the question without context
Allow an answer or an abstention
Record the free-form response

Judge Refusal First
Detect lack-of-knowledge abstention
Corrections still count as attempts
Use an LLM evaluator prompt

Judge Attempted Answers
Compare response with gold answer
Correct · incorrect · unverifiable
Treat the latter two as hallucinated

Report Three Metrics
False refusal rate
Hallucination among attempted answers
Overall correct-answer rate · three trials
